_about: Fly Lab baseline: the lab run of 2026-10-14 (hidden Chrome tab, AMD Radeon integrated GPU, 1638x1135 @1.1). The hub shows these unless this browser has a newer run (localStorage).

A.title: three.js + OpenStreetMap buildings
A.modeNote: 875 buildings · 22k triangles · 3369 trees · 1843 road / path ways

load.detail: From navigation start. Pass ≤ 3 s, partial ≤ 6 s.

frames.detail: 1200 frames of the 291 m route (take-off, between Hyatt Place and MetroPlace, orbit, landing), fixed 1/60 s steps, each frame GPU-synced. Pass: p95 ≤ 16.7 ms (60 fps); partial ≤ 33 ms.

size.detail: map data 0.94 MB · three.js 0.69 MB · lab page 0.12 MB · drone 0.09 MB · fonts 0.00 MB · page 0.00 MB. Compressed bytes over the wire for this visit (includes tiles streamed during the route; cached files still count by their size). Pass ≤ 8 MB, partial ≤ 25 MB.

collide.detail: Full forward stick at Hyatt Place from 62 m out (OSM wall distance), 40 m up. Top speed 15.0 m/s; stopped after 5.4 s; travelled 60.7 m (1.5 m short of the OSM wall). Obstacle probe 0.0 ms per call.

lidar.detail: From a hover in the gap at 40 m: 64 level rays over ±50° towards Hyatt Place + 32 rays sloping down. Ground hits 12, misses 24. Median distance difference to the OSM footprints 0.00 m (n = 60). Mesh raycast (plain THREE.Raycaster, no BVH) against the extruded building meshes, the ground and the guideway (trees and road ribbons left out). A BVH (three-mesh-bvh) would make it far faster. Collision uses the same footprints as 2.5D prisms.

daynight.detail: Our own sky, sun / moon, fog and exposure; lit windows (random per floor and column), a warm street glow on the roads, the drone's nav lights and strobe. Mean frame brightness from the same viewpoint, day then night.

B.modeNote: No key: drone, controls and engine only. Paste a Google Maps Platform key in the box above to load the city.

load.detail: Without a key only the engine and the drone load. From navigation start. Pass ≤ 3 s, partial ≤ 6 s.

frames.detail: 1200 frames of the 291 m route (take-off, between Hyatt Place and MetroPlace, orbit, landing), fixed 1/60 s steps, each frame GPU-synced. Pass: p95 ≤ 16.7 ms (60 fps); partial ≤ 33 ms. Without a key there is no city to draw, so this number is not comparable.

Pass ≤ 8 MB, partial ≤ 25 MB.

collide.detail: Full forward stick at Hyatt Place from 62 m out (OSM wall distance), 40 m up. Top speed 15.0 m/s; stopped after —; travelled 111.9 m (49.7 m past the OSM wall). Obstacle probe 0.0 ms per call.

lidar.detail: From a hover in the gap at 40 m: 64 level rays over ±50° towards Hyatt Place + 32 rays sloping down. Ground hits 0, misses 96. Mesh raycast against the streamed photogrammetry (three.js Raycaster, first hit). The Google mesh carries no building / ground labels: a hit counts as “building” when it is more than 3 m above the pad and on a steep surface.

daynight.detail: The tiles are photographs with daylight and shadows baked in: night is only a blue tint over them (no lit windows, no street lights, shadows stay). Sky, fog and the drone's lights do change. Mean frame brightness from the same viewpoint, day then night. (No key: sky and drone only.)

MapLibre has no 3D raycast: the rays are cast (exactly) against the building polygons of the loaded vector tiles, extruded to render_height, which is the geometry MapLibre draws.

daynight.detail: Night is a re-coloured style (every plain colour in the OpenFreeMap style darkened, MapLibre's light and sky changed). MapLibre has no lighting model for lit windows or street lights; those would need extra hand-made layers. Mean frame brightness from the same viewpoint, day then night.
